description: Typed procedural variables: a value assigned to a DECLAREd variable - through DEFAULT, :=, SELECT INTO or FETCH INTO - is COERCED to the declared type the way Snowflake casts on assignment. Numeric strings parse, fractional values round HALF AWAY FROM ZERO into integral types, a FLOAT holds a double even when assigned an integer, and booleans convert like TO_BOOLEAN. All four assignment paths are pinned, because the coercion is per-path rather than per-variable. SELECT INTO additionally enforces its row and column counts: ZERO rows is NOT an error (verified against live) and simply assigns NULL, which lookup idioms and walk-past-the-end fetch loops rely on; MORE than one row is an error, and an ordinary catchable one; and the number of selected columns must match the number of INTO targets. Converted 1:1 from scripting/SelectIntoCoercionTest (now retired); every coercion claim is read through ::VARCHAR, because the rendered form IS the evidence - 15 rather than 15.0 for an INTEGER target and 1.0 rather than 1 for a FLOAT one - and a JSON number would normalise that distinction away. Its too-many-rows wording test carried an Assumptions.assumeFalse(isLiveSnowflake()) and becomes skip snowflake with the reason kept.

steps.sql: DECLARE t INTEGER; BEGIN SELECT SUM(n) INTO t FROM fives; RETURN t::VARCHAR; END
DECLARE t INTEGER; BEGIN SELECT AVG(n) INTO t FROM nums; RETURN t::VARCHAR; END
DECLARE s VARCHAR; BEGIN SELECT n INTO s FROM one; RETURN s; END
DECLARE x INTEGER DEFAULT '5'; BEGIN RETURN x + 1; END
DECLARE b BOOLEAN DEFAULT 'true'; BEGIN IF (b) THEN RETURN 'yes'; ELSE RETURN 'no'; END IF; END
DECLARE x INTEGER; BEGIN x := '7'; RETURN x + 1; END
DECLARE f FLOAT; BEGIN f := 1; RETURN f::VARCHAR; END
DECLARE t INTEGER; c CURSOR FOR SELECT AVG(n) FROM nums; BEGIN OPEN c; FETCH c INTO t; CLOSE c; RETURN t::VARCHAR; END
DECLARE t INTEGER; BEGIN SELECT n INTO t FROM nums WHERE n > 100; RETURN COALESCE(:t, -1); END

skip.reason: matches the exact 'wrong number of rows: 2' wording of the too-many-rows SELECT INTO error; a real account words that failure differently - the sibling test proves the error itself is raised and catchable on both backends

steps.sql: DECLARE t INTEGER; BEGIN SELECT n INTO t FROM nums; RETURN t; END
DECLARE t INTEGER; BEGIN SELECT n INTO t FROM nums; RETURN t; EXCEPTION WHEN OTHER THEN RETURN 'caught'; END
DECLARE t INTEGER; BEGIN SELECT n, n INTO t FROM one2; RETURN t; END
